name: mc_sightline
title: Line of sight
description:
Tests lines of sight from an eye position: whether specific blocks are visible from there, and what blocks the view if not. Ray tracing uses each block's real shape, so a bottom slab, snow layer, fence or pane only blocks where it has shape; glass, panes, iron bars' gaps and water do not block, leaves do. Read-only.

WHEN TO USE: to answer "can a player see X from here?" (a landmark from spawn, a sign from a path, the funnels from the dock), or to find what is in the way of a view. Mode targets: up to 256 block positions, each answered visible/blocked/unknown with the first blocking block and distances. Mode cone: a coarse grid of first hits over a field of view, to see roughly what fills the view without an image. Pair it with one mc_render view "first-person" only when the user wants to see the view itself.

WHEN NOT TO USE: to check whether a player can walk somewhere or reach a block (sight is not reachability). Not for entities, fog, lighting or render distance: only blocks are traced. Do not use cone mode to inspect exact blocks; use mc_inspect.

PARAMETERS: exactly one of `eye` [x,y,z] (decimals allowed; a standing player's eye is feet y + 1.62) or `player` (their live eye; `world` then comes from the player). Exactly one of `targets` (block positions; each is aimed at its center and at the centers of its faces turned toward the eye, and counts as visible when any of those lines is clear; the target's own cell never blocks) or `cone` {yaw, pitch, fov, rays, distance}: yaw/pitch in Minecraft degrees as F3 shows them (yaw 0 south, 90 west, 180 north, -90 east; pitch -90 up, 90 down), defaulting to the player's direction; fov 10-110 (default 70); rays 4-48 per side (default 24); distance 8-256 (default 128). `ignore` lists blocks that should not block sight, as ids with an optional * wildcard and property conditions, e.g. ["*_leaves", "snow[layers<=3]", "oak_fence"]. Targets must be within 256 blocks of the eye.

SIDE EFFECTS: none - read-only. The server copies only chunks that are already loaded, a few per tick; it never loads chunks, so a line through an unloaded chunk answers unknown (not visible) with the cell where it stopped. Cone output: one character per ray, rows top to bottom: digits 0-9 are the hit distance in tenths of the cone distance, '.' nothing within distance, '?' unknown, plus the most common blocking blocks.

eye.description: Eye position [x, y, z]; decimals allowed. A standing player's eye is feet y + 1.62. Give exactly one of eye or player.

player.description: An online player's name: uses their live eye position and look direction in their own world.

world.description: World name for eye. Omitted uses the plugin's configured default world. Not allowed with player.

targets.description: Block positions to test, each [x, y, z], at most 256, within 256 blocks of the eye.

cone.description: Coarse visibility grid instead of targets.

yaw.description: Default: the player's yaw (required with eye).

pitch.description: Default: the player's pitch (required with eye).

fov.description: Square field of view in degrees, default 70.

ignore.description: Blocks that do not block sight: ids (namespace optional, * wildcard) with optional [prop=value] or numeric [prop<=n] conditions, e.g. "*_leaves", "snow[layers<=3]".
